Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted to our radiation oncology unit complaining of headache, vomiting, and right hemiplegia as part of an intracranial hypertension syndrome. Physical examination revealed a mammary mass in the right breast along with cerebral and lung tumors, bilateral adrenal nodes, and right cerebellar location. The patient underwent total brain irradiation with a dosage of 30 Gray in 10 fractions of 3 Gray per fraction over two weeks, with remarkable improvement in clinical outcomes. The patient was later treated with palliative chemotherapy, which resulted in an incomplete radiological remission of more than 70%. The patient received gemcitabine monotherapy, 1,000 mg/m² on Days 1 and 8 every 21 days after experiencing local breast and cerebral progression. During the follow-up period, the patient's general condition deteriorated rapidly, and they were referred for palliative care and passed away six weeks later.

text:
## Principal diagnosis: **C79.3 – Secondary malignant neoplasm of brain and cerebral meninges**

### Rationale

- **Reason for admission:** The patient presented with headache, vomiting and right hemiplegia, which is an intracranial hypertension syndrome caused by cerebral (including right cerebellar) metastases.
- **Treatment directed at the secondary site:** The main treatment this admission was whole brain irradiation (30 Gy in 10 fractions). Under ACS 0236 (Neoplasm coding and sequencing), when treatment is directed at the metastatic site, the secondary neoplasm is sequenced as principal diagnosis.
- **Symptoms are not coded as principal:** Headache, vomiting and raised intracranial pressure are manifestations of the brain metastases, so they are not assigned as principal diagnosis.
- **Not Z51.0:** This was a symptomatic inpatient admission requiring workup and management. It was not a same-day admission solely for radiotherapy, so Z51.0 (Radiotherapy session) does not apply as principal.

### Likely additional diagnoses

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| C50.9 | Malignant neoplasm of breast, unspecified (male, right breast; use a more specific 4th character if the quadrant is documented) |
| C78.0 | Secondary malignant neoplasm of lung |
| C79.7 | Secondary malignant neoplasm of adrenal gland |
| G81.9 | Hemiplegia, unspecified (code if it meets ACS 0002 criteria) |
| Z51.5 | Palliative care (if provided during this episode) |

**Caveat:** The diagnosis section was withheld. If documentation confirmed a different primary (e.g., a primary lung cancer with breast metastasis), the additional codes would change. The principal diagnosis of C79.3 would still stand, because the admission and treatment were directed at the brain metastases.
